messages:
incident-bot: Paging on-call — Umbracore (tenant: umbracore-prod) dedicated GPU pool at 100% utilization for 12m, queue depth 520, 5xx rate spike to 8%. Auto-scale did not add replicas (max_replicas=4). Alert: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/umbracore

alice_oncall: I’m on it. Looking at infra now — seeing sustained token generation spikes, tail latency climbing. Traces show long queue waits in the scheduling layer.

jamie_sre: @alice_oncall do we have any eviction activity? any preemption logs?

alice_oncall: No evictions yet. Scheduler refused to scale because quota hit; autoscaler says tenant pinned to pool and max_replicas reached.

raja_engops: Confirming — Umbracore has dedicated pool with reserved_capacity=4 gpus, burst_policy=manual. They did not opt into automatic bursting.

marta_support: Umbracore CS: "Customers seeing timeouts and slow responses in production, some 502s." They want ETA.

lucy_pm: This is an enterprise SLA customer. We need immediate mitigation and a comms line. @raja_engops can you advise on burst approval path?

raja_engops: We can do an emergency burst override (temporary extra GPUs) but requires ops approval + brief billing/contract check. Estimated time to provision: ~7–12 minutes after approval. Impact: short-lived additional cost.

jamie_sre: From an SRE standpoint, quickest mitigation: 1) approve burst to add 2 GPUs, 2) throttle non-critical heavy requests with rate-limit rule for Umbracore admin routes, 3) enable fallback to smaller model for high-tokens routes.

alice_oncall: I can push throttling and model fallback now. Will also open provisioning request. Command I’ll run: ```rbctl burst request --tenant umbracore --add-gpus 2 --duration 60m --reason "prod-exhaustion"```

raja_engops: Approved verbally by Ops lead. Please run the request and tag me. I’ll monitor capacity provisioning.

alice_oncall: Running request now. rbctl output: "request accepted, provision in progress (ticket 8943)". Provisioning ETA ~9m.

marta_support: Notifying customer: "We are applying emergency capacity and throttling non-critical paths; will follow up in ~15 minutes with update."

jamie_sre: I pushed a temporary rate-limit rule on route `/v1/generate/stream` -> `x-rate-limit: 50r/s` for that tenant. Also turned on small-model fallback for responses >2048 tokens. Monitor dashboards for error drop.

alice_oncall: Early signs good — queue depth dropping from 520 -> 280 in 3 minutes. 5xx down to 3%.

raja_engops: Provision finished. Extra GPUs online, pool now 6 GPUs. Validation checks passing.

marta_support: Customer updated: "Seeing improvement — thanks."

lucy_pm: Good. Action items: - Follow-up postmortem with root cause (why autoscale didn't add capacity) - Offer Umbracore a retroactive burst discount? - Add playbook step to auto-notify account team on manual-burst tenants.

jamie_sre: I’ll grab metrics and attach logs to the incident. Note: autoscaler refused because burst_policy==manual; we should add a warning in console for tenants at max_replicas and rising queue depth.

alice_oncall: Putting thread into maintenance mode. I’ll remove temporary rate-limits and fallback after traffic stabilizes and burst expires. Will update when finished. :white_check_mark:
